name: Chocolate Blanc-Mange
description: Historical recipe from Common Sense in the Household (1871). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: Cooper's gelatine, soaked in a cup of the milk one hour
ingredients.originalText: 1 oz. Cooper's gelatine, soaked in a cup of the milk one hour

ingredients.name: heaping tablespoonfuls of grated chocolate, rubbed up with a little milk
ingredients.originalText: 4 heaping tablespoonfuls of grated chocolate, rubbed up with a little milk

ingredients.name: eggs, whites and yolks beaten separately
ingredients.originalText: 3 eggs, whites and yolks beaten separately

instructions.text: Heat the milk to boiling; pour in the gelatine and milk, and stir until it is dissolved
Add the sugar to the beaten yolks and stir until smooth
Beat the chocolate into this, and pour in, spoonful by spoonful, the scalding milk upon the mixture, stirring all the while until all is in
Return to the inner saucepan and heat gently, stirring faithfully until it almost boils
Remove from fire, turn into a bowl, and whip in lightly and briskly the beaten whites with the vanilla
Set to form in moulds wet with cold water

source.author: Marion Harland
source.originalInstructions:
1. Heat the milk to boiling; pour in the gelatine and milk, and stir until it is dissolved
2. Add the sugar to the beaten yolks and stir until smooth
3. Beat the chocolate into this, and pour in, spoonful by spoonful, the scalding milk upon the mixture, stirring all the while until all is in
4. Return to the inner saucepan and heat gently, stirring faithfully until it almost boils
5. Remove from fire, turn into a bowl, and whip in lightly and briskly the beaten whites with the vanilla
6. Set to form in moulds wet with cold water
